summary: Cazadero residents built and staffed a lookout on Red Oat Mountain in 1967; it moved to Pole Mountain in 1981 and still stands there.

facts.status_note: The structure moved to Pole Mountain in 1981; the Red Oat Mountain site is listed as gone

events.note: Cazadero citizens built the lookout on Red Oat Mountain
The register says the citizens constructed and staffed the lookout in 1967
Moved from Red Oat Mountain to a better site on Pole Mountain; the Pole Mountain Lookout About page gives the late 1960s instead

corrections.why: The tower moved to Pole Mountain in 1981 and still stands there, so the Red Oat site is a relocation rather than a loss of the structure

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Sonoma Land Trust give 1981; the Pole Mountain Lookout About page says the late 1960s. The story uses 1981 and notes the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: Brief status gone should read relocated: the structure stands at Pole Mountain (see us-ca-pole-mountain). Nothing in the sources describes the Red Oat Mountain site now. Access and staffing today are for the Pole Mountain record: the 2009 visit report predates the 2018 public hiking opening. Move year conflicts across sources (1967 build is consistent). Fact-check 2026-10-10: the Ron Kemnow name was dropped from the citation, because the page does not name him as author.
